name: U2e (mtDNA)
description: Mitochondrial haplogroup U2e is a European and Central Asian subclade of U2 with a notable association with ancient steppe populations. Unlike the South Asian U2a and U2b subclades, U2e has a predominantly Eastern European and Steppe distribution. U2e has been identified in significant frequencies in ancient DNA from Yamnaya and other Bronze Age steppe cultures, positioning it as a marker of the Pontic Steppe people who expanded westward into Europe during the Early Bronze Age. In modern populations, U2e is found at 1–4% across Eastern Europe, the Volga-Ural region, and parts of Siberia, with lower frequencies in Western Europe.
interestingFact: Haplogroup U2e was found in notable frequencies among ancient Yamnaya individuals from the Pontic-Caspian steppe — the population credited with spreading Proto-Indo-European languages into Europe around 5,000 years ago. Its presence in modern Eastern Europeans and Siberians is partly a legacy of this massive Bronze Age migration from the steppe.
references: Haak et al. (2015) — Massive migration from the steppe was a source for Indo-European languages in Europe. Nature 522(7555), 207–211.
Allentoft et al. (2015) — Population genomics of Bronze Age Eurasia. Nature 522(7555), 167–172.
